item.title: Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto Blue Jays
item.description: The Detroit Tigers have already made several significant moves this offseason, but trading Riley Greene would take things to an entirely different level. A new trade proposal involving the Toronto Blue Jays suggests Detroit could part ways with its star outfielder in exchange for a package of four prospects. While there is no indication that the Tigers and Blue Jays are actively discussing this particular trade, the proposed return raises an interesting question about what it would take for Scott Harris to consider moving one of Detroit’s most important offensive players. Earlier this month, Harris addressed the Riley Greene trade rumors , indicating that moving the outfielder was not part of Detroit’s plans. However, that hasn’t stopped outside publications from putting together potential trade packages for the three-time All-Star. Detroit Tigers outfielder Riley Greene (31) stands in the dugout during his game against the Pittsburgh Pirates at Comerica Park in Detroit on Saturday, Sept. 26, 2026. Credit: USA TODAY Network via Reuters Connect (Reuters) Four-Player Trade Proposal Sends Riley Greene to Toronto On Friday, Victor William of Blue Jays Insider examined a three-prospect trade package originally proposed by Motor City Bengals . William suggested Toronto would likely need to include another highly regarded pitching prospect, Nolan Perry, to make the package more enticing. Here is what the hypothetical trade would look like, with prospect rankings courtesy of MLB Pipeline . Detroit Tigers receive: Nolan Perry, RHP (No. 2 prospect) Johnny King, LHP (No. 3 prospect) Blaine Bullard, OF (No. 8 prospect) Ryan Cooney, SS/2B (No. 16 prospect) Toronto Blue Jays receive: – Riley Greene, OF Perry and King would be the headliners of the deal, giving Detroit two of Toronto’s most promising young arms. Bullard would provide the Tigers with an athletic outfield prospect, while Cooney would add another young middle infielder to the organization. Should the Detroit Tigers Consider This Trade? Although acquiring four of Toronto’s top 16 prospects would certainly be intriguing, moving Greene would create an enormous hole in Detroit’s lineup. The 26-year-old outfielder hit .280 during the 2026 season and remains under team control through 2028. The Tigers recently tendered Greene a contract for 2027 , and their aggressive approach to the offseason suggests Harris is interested in building a contender rather than tearing everything down. Trading an established All-Star for four players who have yet to prove themselves at the major league level would seemingly run counter to that approach. It’s an interesting trade proposal, particularly given the upside of Perry and King, but Detroit already has something every organization covets: an established superstar entering his prime. Unless Harris receives an offer that makes the Tigers better both immediately and in the future, Greene should be staying in Detroit.

item.description: Manchester United v Brentford - Premier League 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Callum Wilson has challenged Brentford to secure silverware or European qualification after his clinical double condemned Manchester United to a humiliating 4-0 defeat. The result marks a disastrous Old Trafford debut for Mauricio Pochettino, whose side remain mired in the Premier League relegation zone after another defensive collapse. Wilson leads the charge at Old Trafford Brentford striker Wilson was the architect of Manchester United's downfall on Saturday , netting twice in a dominant first-half display that left the Old Trafford faithful in stunned silence. The experienced forward opened his account for the season in the 19th minute, showing sharp predatory instincts to ghost between two static defenders and convert Dango Ouattara's clever pass. The visitors' second goal arrived just 13 minutes later, again exposing the fragility of Pochettino's backline. Mikkel Damsgaard provided the vision with a pinpoint pass that carved the United defence open, allowing Ouattara to once again turn provider for Wilson. The striker made no mistake with a powerful finish, effectively ending the contest before the interval. Speaking to Sky Sports after the final whistle, Wilson expressed his delight at the result, stating: 'Back-to-back 4-0, which is nice, but it comes down to the hard work that everyone puts in behind the scenes.' The Bees were clinical throughout the afternoon, maintaining their composure even as the home crowd tried to rally behind their new manager. Wilson acknowledged the atmosphere but insisted the team remained focused on their own tactical plan. 'We knew that the crowd would get behind the manager [Mauricio Pochettino] and the team - it was about us playing our own game,' the forward explained. 'It was a nice moment and everyone got to celebrate at the end.' Wilson, meanwhile, is looking towards a bright future for Brentford under the guidance of Keith Andrews. Wilson provided insight into the mentality driving the West London club, noting that despite their relatively small stature, they possess an elite work ethic. 'It is a smaller club that does everything to the maximum of their abilities,' he said. 'Everyone on the inside feels they belong at this level. item.description: Bayern Munich midfielder Joshua Kimmich walks off after his red card against Hamburg on Saturday. (Ibrahim OT) Injury-ravaged Bayern Munich were held to a scoreless draw away at Hamburg in the Bundesliga on Saturday after playing more than half the match with 10 men following captain Joshua Kimmich's sending-off, while Schalke fell to a calamitous 8-1 loss at Paderborn. The draw, Bayern's second in two league games, leaves them a point behind league leaders Borussia Dortmund, who host Bayer Leverkusen on Sunday. Kimmich's moment of madness, being shown a straight red card just before half-time for pulling Alexander Rossing-Lelesiit's hair, is the latest setback in a horror week in the Bavarian capital. "I have to apologise to the team," Kimmich told Sky Germany. "That was very stupid, and it's really not like me at all." Already missing Harry Kane, Jamal Musiala, Michael Olise, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Manuel Neuer and Ismael Saibari, Bayern lost both Lennart Karl and Konrad Laimer to injury in the second half. In addition to their injury woes, club executives have been sharply criticised after launching a public campaign to pressure Musiala to take a pay cut as he struggles with a neurological condition. Bayern lost their first match of the season with a 2-1 defeat away at Lille in the Champions League on Wednesday. Despite the draw, Bayern coach Vincent Kompany was upbeat after the match and praised his charges. "Given the current situation, if they keep fighting like this, then it's actually a real joy to be their coach," Kompany told DAZN. "We just have to respect this phase and approach it the right way." - Bayern decimated - Coming into the match, decimated Bayern had won 14 of their past 16 matches with Hamburg and had not tasted defeat against them since 2009. Clear goal chances were few and far between for both sides in the second half, with Bayern's appeals for a stoppage-time penalty for a foul on Luis Diaz waved away. The Bavarian giants will look to get back to winning ways when they host high-flying Hertha Berlin, who are on track for promotion after winning 12 of their 13 Bundesliga 2 games this season, in the German Cup on Tuesday. item.title: Pittsburgh Steelers: NFL insider reveals what Mike McCarthy will do differently after Aaron Rodgers exit
item.description: The Pittsburgh Steelers entered play on Friday with a 6-4 record and an unprecedented quarterback controversy. Earlier in the week, four-time NFL MVP Aaron Rodgers sent head coach Mike McCarthy an ultimatum: either he himself call the offensive plays on the field or he was going to quit the team. McCarthy and the Steelers called his bluff, announcing that the future Hall of Famer would be benched and inactive for Friday’s game. Instead of taking the consequence, Rodgers doubled down. He went on the Pat McAfee Show and aired a great deal of grievances against McCarthy. He claimed that the head coach fell asleep in meetings, had an assistant dedicated solely to bringing him ice cream sandwiches, and that he did not have a good enough relationship with the defensive players. Pittsburgh responded by releasing Rodgers, and no NFL team wants to sign him for the home stretch of the season. In short, his career is over. Meanwhile, McCarthy is not taking the criticism lightly. Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy is taking a humble approach to the controversy Nov 27, 2026; Pittsburgh, Pennsylvania, USA; Pittsburgh Steelers head coach Mike McCarthy looks on during the first half against the Denver Broncos at Acrisure Stadium. While much of what he said should be taken with a grain of salt given his history of burning bridges, it is also true that the Steelers head coach can be better. And he knows it. According to ESPN insider Jeremy Fowler, McCarthy sat down with the defensive players specifically to address whatever concerns they have regarding their relationship with him. “I was told [McCarthy] was humbled by all this,” Fowler said . “And talking to sources within the building, it’s not like Mike McCarthy just didn’t work at all. item.title: Lakers schedule filled out after getting knocked out of NBA Cup
item.description: After the Lakers were knocked out of the NBA Cup , the previously unknown parts of their regular-season schedule were revealed on Friday night, featuring a first-time matchup and a familiar opponent. The league announced the Lakers will travel to Oklahoma City to play the Thunder on Dec. 6 and host the Jazz on Dec. 10 for the two games added to their schedule. The Lakers will get their first matchup against the Thunder since last season’s playoffs. Getty Images The Lakers were eliminated from the NBA Cup after Friday’s road loss to the Spurs, with the Mavericks, Trail Blazers, Grizzlies and Thunder advancing to the Knockout Rounds from the Western Conference. The Lakers-Thunder matchup will now be the first of four games between the teams, with previously scheduled games on Jan. 26 and March 6 in Los Angeles and April 1 in Oklahoma City. The Thunder, led by reigning back-to-back MVP Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, swept the Luka Doncic-less Lakers out of the playoffs in the second round in the spring to end their season before falling to the Spurs in seven games in the Western Conference finals. They’ve been without Chet Holmgren, Jalen Williams and Cason Wallace since the trio sustained their respective injuries against the Clippers on Oct. 25. The Lakers have a 2-1 series lead over the Jazz. AP Photo/Kyusung Gong The matchup against the Jazz and Lakers will be the fourth and final regular-season meeting between the teams. The game on Dec. 10 will be the third game in three weeks, with the Lakers falling to the Jazz on Nov. 18 to end their nine-game winning streak before beating the Jazz on Nov. 23 , with both games being in Los Angeles. The Lakers beat the Jazz on Oct. 25 in Salt Lake City for their third straight win to open the season.

item.title: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford
item.description: 0 crosses, 0 dribbles, 1 big chance missed: Patrick Dorgu’s costly nightmare leaves Man United paying the price vs. Brentford Patrick Dorgu endured a game to forget as Manchester United suffered a humiliating 4-0 defeat to Brentford on Saturday. Thrashed Mauricio Pochettino’s Old Trafford debut proved to be a nightmare as he and his players were well and truly beaten by Brentford, marking their first victory at United’s iconic home since 1937. United started brightly as they dominated possession and created chances. But they failed to make it count and were ruthlessly punished. The deadlock was broken by Callum Wilson, who gathered the ball just outside the area, spun away from United’s defenders and fired past Senne Lammens. Wilson doubled Brentford’s lead not too long after with an easy tap-in from a cross. Pochettino made changes at half-time, bringing on Luke Shaw and Bryan Mbeumo in place of Lisandro Martinez and Amad. The substitutions failed to provide any spark, as United’s response was cumbersome and fruitless. In United’s search for a breakthrough, Joshua Zirkzee lifted his effort over, Dorgu had a shot batted away, and Youri Tielemans came closest of all with an effort that clipped the crossbar. A Harry Maguire header was also stopped on the line, while substitute Shea Lacey also tested the goalkeeper with a powerful shot. But Brentford went on to secure the win in the 82nd minute as Kristoffer Ajer reacted the quickest to slam home from a corner kick. Kevin Schade then piled further misery on United with a cheeky lobbed finish. United remain in 19th place in the Premier League table and could end the matchweek at rock bottom if Crystal Palace beat Hull City on Sunday. Dorgu’s performance Pochettino elected to deploy Dorgu on the left of the attack in preference to Matheus Cunha, a decision that did not prove beneficial. Dorgu wasted several opportunities, and it could be argued that had he converted at least one, the outcome might have looked different for United. In 70 minutes on the field, Dorgu attempted three shots, just one of them on target. He ought to have done much better with the opportunity provided by Fernandes but could not get past Kelleher. He managed an individual shot accuracy of just 33.3%. found a United teammate with 14 of the 17 passes he attempted (82.4% pass accuracy). Dorgu failed to complete the one dribble he embarked on. He also did not contribute a tackle or interception. However, he won six of the eight duels he delved into. He also won three fouls. United are next in action on Wednesday when they face Newcastle at St James’ Park.

item.title: Huge boost for Hansi Flick! Barcelona welcome back three stars for Deportivo trip
item.description: Real Betis Balompie v FC Barcelona - LaLiga EA Sports 2026/27 - Getty Images Sport Barcelona have received a major triple injury boost ahead of Sunday's Liga trip to Deportivo A Coruna, with Lamine Yamal, Rodri, and Andreas Christensen all declared fit to return. Triple boost for Barcelona ahead of Deportivo Yamal, Rodri, and Christensen are all back in contention for Barca's away fixture against Deportivo on Sunday. Their availability provides a timely lift for the Catalan side following a demanding stretch of fixtures. Yamal sat out the midweek Champions League victory at Sabah in Baku, Azerbaijan, due to an ankle problem . That long journey marked the first match the teenager has missed for Barcelona all season. Rodri has also recovered from the hamstring injury he sustained in the win over Aston Villa on November 3. The midfielder missed Barcelona's last three matches as well as two Spain fixtures during the November international break, while Christensen returns after missing two games with a calf issue. Flick confirms returns amid fresh injury blows Speaking on Saturday, Flick confirmed that the returning trio are ready to feature. However, the Barcelona coach must also contend with new absences, as both Alejandro Balde and Marc Bernal have been ruled out. "Rodri, Andreas and also Lamine, they travel with us and they can play," Flick told reporters. "Marc has some problems, it's not a big injury. We have to see. But he's out for [Deportivo] and also maybe next game against Atletico [Madrid]." Fermín suspension opens door for Olmo Yamal's swift recovery is vital for Blaugrana, given he started every Liga and Champions League fixture prior to midweek, registering 13 goals and 13 assists in 17 appearances. Rodri had likewise been a fixture in the side, playing 14 successive matches before his injury, whereas Christensen has managed just one 30-minute outing against Atletico Madrid earlier this month. Alongside long-term absentees Xavi Espart and Roony Bardghji, Barcelona are also without Fermin Lopez. The midfielder is serving a two-game suspension following his red card against Villarreal last weekend, leaving Dani Olmo to step up. Crucial week ahead for Flick's side Barcelona travel to face Deportivo on Sunday aiming to make the most of Yamal and Rodri's return to the starting picture. item.title: Kyle Whittingham contract buyout: What would firing cost Michigan?
item.description: Kyle Whittingham's contract buyout if he were to be fired at Michigan football would cost the university $24.75 million. Whittingham's future remains cloudy, with the Wolverines at 6-5 overall and 3-5 in the Big Ten standings , entering their rivalry game Saturday, Nov. 28, at unranked Ohio State . It's Michigan's worst full season since going 5-7 in 2014 , Brady Hoke's final season. Whittingham's chances of returning did not look good as recently as a week ago, when the university signed a memorandum of understanding with Trev Alberts to hire him away from Texas A&M as its new athletic director. But chaos reigns at Michigan and the university backed out of the deal by Tuesday. This has Whittingham's chances looking better to continue as coach in 2027. "The likelihood is to [keep] Kyle," one person with knowledge of the situation told the Free Press this week. "Circumstances around the AD are such that it's complicated and hard to make a change [immediately]." EXCLUSIVE: Inside Michigan AD debacle, what's next and Kyle Whittingham's future The 2027 recruiting class has early signing day scheduled for next week, Wednesday-Friday (Dec. 2-4), which makes a decision by current AD Warde Manuel, who still has authority , and others extremely pressing. Whittingham, 68, signed a five-year deal in December 2025 worth $41 million, according to his contract obtained by the Free Press as first reported on Nov. 8. Per that contract, if U-M relieves him of duties at any point during that window, he is owed an "amount equivalent to 75% of the Head Coach's Base Salary in monthly installments for the remainder of the scheduled Term of this Agreement." He's set to be paid $33 million over the next four years, which would mean a buyout would cost $24.75 million. The deal says he's required to seek immediate employment, but it's more likely this would be a retirement given his age and where he's at in his career; it's unclear how that would impact the buyout, if at all. The nearly $25 million is a drop in the bucket in the grand scheme of U-M spending, but it would be the department's latest eight-figure amount that goes toward something off the field. Michigan is still finishing payments of more than $30 million in NCAA fines for a sign-stealing scandal , recently paid more than $12 million to a law firm for an internal review of its athletic department culture , and has a athletic director search nightmare on its hands, after bungling its decision to hire Alberts, than backing out . That decision could force the university to have to pay Alberts up to $17 million and it is also on the hook to pay $4 million to buy Alberts' contract at Texas A&M, a position from which he resigned after signing with U-M. item.title: Louisville honors Tom Jackson with special helmet decal
item.description: The sports world continues to pay tribute to Tom Jackson nearly a week after his death on Nov. 20 at age 75. The former Denver Broncos linebacker and longtime ESPN broadcaster built his football foundation at the University of Louisville, where he played from 1970 to 1972 before becoming a fourth-round pick in the 1973 NFL Draft. Jackson’s college roots ran deep with the Cardinals. His No. 50 jersey was honored by Louisville in 1999, recognizing a career that helped put the program on the map before his Pro Bowl and broadcasting success. That connection was on full display Saturday. The tribute places Jackson alongside a short list of program legends recognized with in-game helmet honors, a gesture reserved for players who left a lasting mark on Louisville football. item.title: Ducks Wire staff predicts Oregon Ducks vs. Washington Huskies
item.description: Rivalry week is finally here, and for the Oregon Ducks , everything is on the line. With a win over the Washington Huskies , Oregon can keep its season alive, likely grabbing a spot in the Big Ten Championship Game, or an at-large bid into the College Football Playoff, at the very least. With a loss, though, the postseason dreams would come crashing down after an awe-inspiring comeback over the past month. Talk about motivation for the Huskies to come into Autzen Stadium and ruin the party, right? To preview the game, we go through our weekly roundtable with the writers from Ducks Wire to offer our opinions and predictions for what's to come. Here is our roundtable conversation. Michigan State Reaction Question: Well, that was about as stress-free as it gets. Oregon demolished Michigan State 45-7 on Friday night, winning its fourth straight game and continuing one of the more remarkable midseason turnarounds we've seen in recent memory. What was your biggest takeaway from that win, and what impressed you most about the Ducks ' performance? Zachary Neel: I think the ability to weather an early injury was impressive. With Dierre Hill going out on the third snap of the game, Brandon Smith came in and had a career day, showing the depth of talent that the Ducks have in the backfield. A blowout win was expected over Michigan State, but the way in which the Ducks did it resonated with me. Don Smalley: I was impressed they played a complete game this time and on the road. Michigan State isn't great, but they do have the capability to bite you and Oregon never let them. Bjorn Bergstrom: My biggest takeaway was just that the Ducks looked like the Ducks: beating up on lower competition teams with ease. That’s not the Oregon squad that we saw a month ago against Illinois, but the Ducks have done it two weeks in a row against the Michigan programs. While it’d be a stretch to say that they look like the preseason No. 2 team that they were, they’re right there. Saturday morning brought us a new day for another match where Manchester United folded under the weight of their own mistakes. Self-inflicted wounds and a pair of atrocious first half concessions put a positive opening 15 minutes to waste for the Reds. Whatever structure was established by Mauricio Pochettino going into the match was apparent with a forward-thinking approach to start the match. A better front three likely would have capitalized on the potential to create chances. Instead, it was simple saves and off-target shots and crosses. On the other end, Callum Wilson scored a brace for the visitors to kickstart their first win at Old Trafford as a Premier League side. The veteran forward scored his first with a touch past an off-balance Maguire and a shot dead center that Senne Lammens didn’t react to in time. Wilson’s second was a tap-in, served up to him on a plate by Ouattara, who embarrassed Lisandro Martinez with a simple cutback and then squared the ball through Maguire’s legs to find him. Within 15 minutes, the opening 15 minutes meant nothing, and the Reds had made it eight consecutive performances having conceded at least two goals. There were a few more positive stretches in the second half, but there wasn’t near enough to find the net. The best shots on target came from substitute Shea Lacey having a go, demonstrating the kind of ambition and eye for making things happen that was sorely lacking from the starting group of Joshua Zirkzee, Patrick Dorgu and Amad. The three points were sealed by the visitors with a pair of dagger goals in the final minutes, ensuring another week sinking into the relegation zone for United with an Old Trafford crowd demanding change at the top. Embarrassing and weak from a once great club.

item.title: Bayern Munich’s Vincent Kompany: ‘It wasn’t a penalty’
item.description: Photo by Selim Sudheimer/Getty Images | Getty Images Bayern Munich could perhaps have squeaked a win in their away Bundesliga match against Hamburger SV. Though the team had been reduced to 10 men for the entire second half following Joshua Kimmich’s red card, they managed to stay in the game and maintain the 0-0 score line. Then, as the match entered the last minute of added time, Luis Díaz burst into the box and was brought to the ground under pressure from multiple opponents, only for the referee to judge the challenges as fair and whistle a foul against Díaz. Perhaps, on another day, the call would have been a foul on Díaz, a penalty for Bayern and a chance out of nowhere to steal all three points. If that happened, though, head coach Vincent Kompany believes it would have been the wrong call. “It wasn’t a penalty, and it wasn’t a foul against Luis Díaz,” Kompany stated plainly (as captured by @iMiaSanMia ) before explaining his thinking. “There was no real contact. Why do I say it wasn’t a penalty? His foot goes into the ground, and then… you simply cannot award a penalty for something like that. No, no complaints from me. Of course, you can always have a different opinion here and there, and we certainly have ours as well. I don’t want to talk too much about it.” That penalty could have altered the course of the match late on, but Bayern and Hamburg ultimately settled for a draw after a chaotic end to the game. item.description: Mercedes deputy team principal Bradley Lord is hoping Kimi Antonelli and George Russell can capitalise on what has been a dominant weekend for the Silver Arrows so far, with the pair once again comfortably clear of the competition in FP3 at the Qatar Grand Prix. All signs point towards a potential Mercedes front-row lockout in qualifying, reminiscent of the early stages of the season, when Russell and Antonelli regularly found themselves battling each other for pole position. Lord urges Mercedes to deliver when it matters in Qatar Speaking to Sky Sports at the end of FP3, Lord stressed the importance of carrying that momentum into qualifying and Sunday's Grand Prix, having failed to capitalise on Mercedes' potential in recent weekends. “It’s looked pretty good so far. We’ve done it in all the sessions that don’t matter, and now we’ve got to go out and do the job when it counts in qualifying and then tomorrow in the Grand Prix. “The last couple (of weekends) haven’t really come together. We’ve been in position to be on the podium or winning the races and haven’t done so.” Photo: Race Pictures Photo: Race Pictures Lord also explained why the characteristics of the Lusail circuit appear to suit the Mercedes so well, particularly compared to some of the corners in Brazil and Las Vegas. “Here, there are lots of high and medium speed corners, the car’s clearly very comfortable there. Smooth tarmac, and both drivers performing very, very strongly. “It certainly seems to suit us. The car’s been a bit weaker in the slow speed, as we saw in Vegas, as we saw in some parts of the circuit in Brazil. So, it’s playing to our strengths, but both drivers are doing a really good job with it.” Mercedes also appeared to have the upper hand over its rivals during Friday's long runs, although Sunday's Grand Prix will present an unusual strategic challenge. item.title: Benching Austin Jackson Is The Only Move Left For Miami
item.description: Credit: David Santiago-Imagn Images The Miami Dolphins sit at 1-9 and need to make a bold move. Austin Jackson is not the answer at right tackle anymore. He has missed time due to injury and played inconsistently all season. The team has new options ready to step in. Head coach Jeff Hafley said Jackson has performed worse this season than in previous years. General Manager Jon-Eric Sullivan wants a tough, physical line built from the inside out. Sullivan identified Patrick Paul and Aaron Brewer as the core players for this future. He also drafted Kadyn Proctor to play right tackle but moved him to left guard. Now, the door is open to switch Proctor back to right tackle. The Dolphins traded for Caeden Wallace as a swing tackle, yet he has been inactive in recent games. Starting Wallace or Proctor makes sense when the team has nothing to lose. The Case for a Change Jackson was expected to be a cornerstone player when he got drafted in 2020. Instead, he has become a liability on the offensive line. The Dolphins could not even trade him at the deadline for a future late-round pick. That shows the rest of the NFL does not value him highly. He knows he might not be on the team next year. Sitting him now gives the front office a clear look at what they have for the future. Due to knee and elbow injuries, Jackson has been limited in practice, according to Yahoo Sports . “Like most players there are bumps and bruises he is battling through,” Hafley said. “He’s doing everything he can to get ready to play.” But being ready does not mean playing well. The team needs to see if the younger guys can handle the pressure better than a struggling veteran. Jackson was downgraded to DNP on Friday’s final report. Who Steps In Next? If the Dolphins move Proctor to right tackle, they leave left guard open. The team features Jarrett Kingston, who has played well whenever they called on him. They also keep DJ Campbell on the practice squad, a player they drafted themselves. These options are worth a shot. The team can fill the open roster spot with veterans like Ronnie Harrison, who is in consideration to be activated. This is a time to test the depth and find the right pieces. Jeff Hafley said, according to Orlando Sentinel , “We’ll figure out who exactly that starter is going into Sunday.” The Dolphins face the New York Jets on Sunday, Nov. 29, at 1 p.m. ET at Hard Rock Stadium.

item.title: The Galaxy keep missing the playoffs. Fans want ownership to take action
item.description: Galaxy forward Kyogo Furuhashi reacts during a match against Seattle at Dignity Health Sports Park on Sept. 12. After winning the MLS Cup title in 2024, the Galaxy haven't returned to the playoffs. (Luiza Moraes / Getty Images) Statistically, it’s far easier to make the MLS playoffs than it is to miss them. Eighteen of 30 teams qualify for the postseason, meaning each one starts the season with a 60% chance of making the playoffs. No other major professional sports league in the U.S. is as generous. Yet the Galaxy failed to make the cut this year. And last year. In fact, the Galaxy have missed the playoffs four times in six years since Greg Vanney took over as manager. They also missed in three of the four seasons before Vanney arrived, meaning the Galaxy have cleared the lowest playoff bar in American sports just three times in the last decade. And they haven’t done it in consecutive seasons since Bruce Arena was the coach. Read more: Mauricio Pochettino's exit places U.S. men's soccer in a precarious state Arena left a decade ago. (To be fair, the last time the Galaxy did reach the playoffs, in 2024, Vanney guided them to a championship .) But wait, there’s more. Home attendance was down, dropping below the 20,000 per-game average for the first time in a non-COVID season since the Galaxy left the Rose Bowl for Carson in 2003. That’s a decrease of more than 18% since 2023. All this should be concerning for the team and its owners at AEG. The Galaxy, after all, used to be the model MLS franchise. It won the most games, had the best players, collected the most titles and led the league in attendance nine times. Today? Not so much. So does AEG have a plan to fix that? We reached out to Dan Beckerman , AEG’s president and chief executive, through a company spokesman, hoping for some clues. We never heard back. However, general manager Will Kuntz , speaking in a videoconference with the media Friday, agreed things are dismal. “I don’t think we did a good enough job collectively last year,” he said. “So for us, it’s really about taking a hard look at everything we’ve done process-wise and saying ‘hey, how can we be better?’ Because it cannot continue like this.” Galaxy coach Greg Vanney reacts during a match against LAFC at BMO Stadium on Oct. 25. (Luke Hales / Getty Images) Yet Kuntz, the architect of the MLS Cup team, may not be around to see that process through. Vanney still has two years left on his lucrative contract while Kuntz’s deal ends next month, so if there’s going to be a fall guy for the Galaxy’s recent failures, it’s likely to be the GM, not the coach. On Friday, Kuntz was already speaking of the team in the past tense. “I really enjoyed my time at the Galaxy. I love being here,” he said. “I’d like to be back if it was up to me. By the World Cup break, 15 games in, they’d only added two more. There needed to be changes, and they needed to be big. The Crew general manager moved quickly. In May, he fired coach Henrik Rydström, his first coaching hire as the Crew’s chief soccer officer, though he was quick to point out he was involved with previous hires including bringing in Wilfried Nancy. He spent big in the summer, revamping the Crew’s attack and adding pieces while bidding farewell to some regulars. Ten players arrived, and eight went out. It worked. The Crew turned the boat around, going from worst in the Eastern Conference to closing the season on a six-game win streak and having won eight of their last nine. That was enough not only to jump out of Thursday’s wild card match but to set up a First Round playoff series with Inter Miami, the reigning champion led by Lionel Messi. They also pushed to the U.S. Open Cup final, falling to St. Louis City in a penalty shootout. All of it led Tall to believe he made the right decisions, moving on quickly from the coach he thought was the right man for the job. “Some people could’ve waited the full year. Maybe it would’ve been safer, but that’s not me. That’s not us as a club. That’s not even the way we play!” Tall told USA TODAY Sports ahead of the playoffs. “You see how we are bold and are not afraid of taking risk. At the end of the day, it wasn’t even a risk necessarily. It was necessary for our players, for our club as a whole and I think ultimately we made the right decision to do it at that time.” Tall still stands by Rydström as a good coach, something he’s proving while leading Hammarby in Sweden which currently sits atop of the table after running off five consecutive wins. item.title: Beckham to be inducted into US Soccer Hall of Fame
item.description: David Beckham was knighted by King Charles in 2025 [Getty Images] David Beckham will be inducted into the United States' National Soccer Hall of Fame as part of its 2027 class. The former Manchester United and England midfielder, 51, made headlines in 2007 when he moved to Los Angeles from Spanish giants Real Madrid to join Major League Soccer (MLS) side LA Galaxy on a five-year contract. He made 124 appearances in all competitions for Galaxy, scoring 20 goals, and twice won both the MLS Cup and Supporters' Shield. Beckham's six seasons at Galaxy helped to raise the global profile of MLS and following his retirement in 2013, he became co-owner of MLS club Inter Miami, who signed Argentina World Cup winner Lionel Messi in 2023. His induction ceremony is set to take place on 16 April 2027 in Frisco, Texas. David Beckham's deal with LA Galaxy in 2007 was reportedly worth £128m [Getty Images] He was told the news he had been chosen on the veterans' ballot at an MLS board of governors' meeting on Thursday and said his time in the US has been "an incredible journey". Beckham, who had two loan spells with AC Milan in 2009 and 2010 while at Galaxy, added: "I'm looking to build this league and this sport in this great country for a long time." Meanwhile, former US internationals Megan Rapinoe and Julie Ertz have also been voted into the Hall of Fame in their first year of eligibility. Ballon d'Or winner Rapinoe, 41, and midfielder Ertz, 34, lifted the Women’s World Cup twice with with the US in 2015 and 2019. "To be alongside all the greatest players that have played for us, and played for our country alongside a bunch of my team-mates and friends, recognised like that in this way just means you were successful and a part of great teams," Rapinoe wrote on Instagram.
